reasoning: Both remove the replicated server parts, send only on change at about 20/s, and draw ghosts on each client. A puts ghost updates on UnreliableRemoteEvents, uses sequence numbers to discard stale updates, sends a full resend every second to repair dropped ones, and interpolates against server timestamps. B keeps ghost traffic on reliable RemoteEvents, which the rubric specifically flags, and does not justify that choice. A's write-up is also more thorough. B's one advantage, silence when idle, does not outweigh this.

criteria.note: reportOwnGhost sends only when GhostCodec.isSame says the state changed, at most every SEND_INTERVAL (40 ms, so 25/s) whatever the frame rate; an unchanged state is still resent every RESEND_INTERVAL (1/s), so an idle builder is not fully silent.

criteria.criterion: Ghosts built on each client; server only relays
criteria.note: The server keeps no parts and only sends GhostBatch buffers; clients create parts in a local GhostPreviews folder and draw them a short delay behind, gliding between timestamped samples.

criteria.criterion: Own ghost drawn locally every frame
criteria.note: onRenderStepped calls drawOwnGhost(getCursorState()) every frame with no server round trip.

MoveGhost and GhostBatch are both UnreliableRemoteEvents, with sequence checks (isNewerSequence), a full resend every second, and the 1,000-byte cap handled via MaxEntriesPerBatch; placement files are untouched.

decodeMove checks the type and exact buffer length and rejects unknown block indices, and i16 coordinates rule out NaN; there is no explicit per-player rate limit (the relay is capped at one entry per batch), FireAllClients echoes to the builder but the client drops its own slot, and ghosts are destroyed on PlayerRemoving and hidden when the block index is 0.

Thorough per-message math, before/after table, scaling with player count and a verification plan, plus a good list of what players will notice; one line says byte costs come from a Studio measurement while the doc also says nothing has been run.
All checks pass; changes are limited to the two scripts, the doc and a shared GhostCodec module, and the code is well typed.
updateOwnGhost returns early when GhostCodec.equals reports no change and throttles to SendInterval (20/s), so an idle client sends nothing.

criteria.criterion: Ghosts built on each client; server only relays
criteria.note: The server only batches the dirty slots into GhostUpdates; clients create LocalGhosts parts and ease them toward each new target with exponential smoothing.

criteria.criterion: Own ghost drawn locally every frame
criteria.note: updateOwnGhost runs every RenderStepped and moves ownGhost straight from the cursor cell.
GhostState and GhostUpdates are reliable RemoteEvents, so ghost traffic still shares the ordered reliable stream, and the write-up never explains the choice; PlaceBlock is untouched.

decodeState checks the type, length and block index; there is no explicit rate limit (relay coalesced via the dirty table), the builder's own updates are echoed and filtered on the client, and the ghost is hidden via dirty on leave but the client part is never destroyed.
Clear assumptions marked as estimates, before/after math and a summary table, a good list of what players will notice, and tuning notes.
All checks pass and the scope is tight; the own ghost's block type is reapplied every frame and the late-join snapshot depends on the client's first send.

strengths: Unreliable transport with sequence ordering and a periodic full resend
Interpolation against server timestamps, with handling for pauses
Thorough, honest write-up with a verification plan
Handles the unreliable payload size limit
weaknesses: Idle builders resend once per second
No explicit per-player rate limit on incoming messages
Updates are echoed to the builder and filtered on the client
Write-up wording about the byte costs being 'measured' is slightly ambiguous
Ghost traffic stays on reliable RemoteEvents, against the core goal
Remote ghost parts are hidden rather than destroyed when the player leaves
Easing toward the latest cell is less steady than timestamped interpolation
